model.reason: no model; this audits the measuring instrument itself

kernel.probed: tg256_ept2, tg512_ept1, tg1024_ept4 -- three forge variants

result.why_this_was_run: the bandit receipt noticed the same candidate failed the reliability gate at 13.56% IQR in one run and passed at 3.19% in another. Every performance claim in this program rests on that gate, so the gate's own input being noisy is worth measuring rather than noting.
result.method: 8 INDEPENDENT IQR estimates per candidate per rep count, at 20/40/100/200 reps
result.the_finding: AT 20 AND 40 REPS THE GATE VERDICT FLIPS FOR EVERY CANDIDATE PROBED. tg256_ept2's IQR estimate ranged 1.84%-13.38% across eight 20-rep runs and 3.41%-14.29% across eight 40-rep runs -- the same kernel judged reliable or unreliable depending on which run you happened to do. At 100 reps two of three still flip. At 200 reps all three hold inside a 3-point band and no verdict flips.

what_it_means_for_earlier_work.large_margin_conclusions_stand: P5 fusion 1.71x, P6 unified memory 7.4x, P7 native 2.08x, atomics 3.05x and the GEMM results all rest on MARGINS far larger than any plausible IQR error. Those do not move.
what_it_means_for_earlier_work.reliability_verdicts_at_low_reps_are_sus: the original forge run BARRED three candidates for failing the gate at ~25 reps -- tg128_ept2, tg512_ept1 and tg1024_ept4. Two of those three are probed here and their TRUE IQR sits near 5%, comfortably inside the gate. They were most likely barred BY NOISE IN THE MEASUREMENT OF NOISE, not by being unrepeatable.
what_it_means_for_earlier_work.borderline_no_claims_are_suspect: any NO_CLAIM driven by an arm sitting near the 10% line at low reps could have gone either way. The verdicts driven by large margins are unaffected.

result.the_fix: time_arm now reports reliability_verdict_is_stable and attaches a caveat below 200 reps, so a `reliable` flag taken from too few samples cannot be cited as a property of the kernel. A test pins both branches.
result.what_it_costs: a stable reliability verdict needs 200 reps where the program has typically used 20-60. That is 3-10x the measurement budget for any claim whose admission depends on the gate rather than on a large margin.

claim_boundary: Three kernels, one shape, one machine, eight estimates per cell. This establishes that MY OWN GATE is unstable below roughly 200 reps on THIS workload; it does not establish a universal threshold, and a different kernel with genuinely bimodal timing could be unstable at any rep count. It does NOT overturn any large-margin result. It DOES mean the forge's three barred candidates were probably barred wrongly, and that is recorded against the forge rather than quietly fixed.
